content.passage: Omar loved designing things. One day, his teacher gave the class a challenge: “How can we make life easier for new students at school?” Omar had a few ideas, but his teacher stopped him. “First, see through their eyes,” she said. “You need to understand how they feel.” So Omar spent a day with a new student named Karim. He watched Karim closely. Karim didn’t talk much. He looked confused and nervous. He didn’t know where to sit or what to do during the break. Omar felt sorry. He remembered how hard it was when he was new. Later, Omar and his group wrote down everything they noticed. Then they brainstormed ideas. They created a “Welcome Buddy” plan, a school map for new students, and a break-time corner for newcomers. When they tested the idea, the new students smiled and felt more relaxed. Omar learned something important: Good design starts with real people—and real feelings.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Hi Magdy, do you know what design thinking is?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: It’s a way to solve problems by doing some steps. First, you must understand the users and what they need. This part might take some time, but it’s important.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Next, think of many ideas. Be creative and don’t worry about being perfect.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Then, you should make a simple model or drawing called a prototype.

dialogue.speaker: Magdy
dialogue.text: Is it okay if it’s not perfect?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Yes! Design thinking is a process where you improve your prototype many times.

dialogue.speaker: Magdy
dialogue.text: That makes sense. What happens after making the prototype?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Finally, test it and ask people what they think. Then, fix it and make it better. Keep it practical and useful.

dialogue.speaker: Magdy
dialogue.text: Thanks! So, first understand, then brainstorm, next make a prototype, and keep improving it.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Exactly! If you do this, you might make something really great.
